career_ladder.note: Ordinary Grade Drivers and Mechanical Technical Staff in the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Ministry of Mines, operate and maintain 4x4 heavy field expedition trucks, drilling equipment carriers, mobile laboratories, and specialized survey jeeps across rugged terrains, remote desert tracts, and high-altitude Himalayan geological missions. Governed by Central Civil Services rules and GSI Technical Staff Service Rules, progression follows a structured four-grade driver hierarchy based on qualifying service and trade tests.

steps.years: Entry Grade (₹19,900 - ₹63,200), Group C Non-Gazetted (probation 2 years)
steps.source_label: GSI Driver (Ordinary Grade) Recruitment Rules & Regional Advertisements

steps.years: approx. 9 years (Promoted on completion of 9 years regular service in Ordinary Grade subject to passing trade test)
steps.source_label: Staff Car Driver / Field Driver Hierarchy Rules, Ministry of Mines

steps.years: approx. 15 years (Promoted after 6 years regular service in Grade-II)
approx. 18-20 years (Senior non-gazetted technical grade per DoPT Staff Car Driver scheme)
steps.source_label: DoPT Staff Car Driver Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) & Special Grade Scheme

steps.years: approx. 25+ years (Selection post for fleet management and mechanical workshop supervision)

exam_scheme.note: Recruitment is organized regional-wise (Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, Central, and North Eastern Regions) through a two-stage examination: a Written Examination (100 marks objective OMR test) followed by a mandatory Practical Driving and Automotive Mechanical Trade Test.

stages.source_label: GSI Scheme of Examination for Ordinary Grade Drivers and Mechanical Staff

papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for UR, 35% for OBC/EWS, 30% for SC/ST across aggregate written examination

papers.paper_name: Traffic Rules, Motor Vehicles Act & Road Safety Signs
Vehicle Mechanisms, Routine Maintenance, Engine Diagnostics & Troubleshooting
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% marks required in vehicle mechanisms section

stages.source_label: GSI Trade Test Guidelines for Driver (Ordinary Grade)

papers.paper_name: Practical Driving Assessment (Heavy / Light Vehicle Maneuvering, Reversing, Rough Terrain & Hill Driving)
papers.negative_marking: Evaluated on obstacle course driving, reverse parking, and rough track navigation
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 50% marks required to qualify; qualifying in nature

papers.paper_name: Mechanical Maintenance and On-Spot Fault Rectification Test
papers.negative_marking: Hands-on assessment of tyre changing, engine oil checks, fan belt tensioning, fuse replacements, and battery maintenance

financial_package.pay_source_label: 7th CPC Pay Matrix Level 2 (₹19,900 - ₹63,200) for Driver (Ordinary Grade) in GSI
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated for Level 2 entry basic pay of ₹19,900. Dearness Allowance at canonical 58% equals ₹11,542. House Rent Allowance ranges from ₹1,990 (10% in Z-class rural/camp stations) to ₹5,970 (30% in X-class cities like Kolkata CHQ, Hyderabad, Delhi). Transport Allowance ranges from ₹1,422 to ₹2,133. Field staff deployed in remote mineral prospecting camps receive additional Special Camp Allowance and Daily Allowance for geological expedition tours. Deductions include NPS 10% (Basic + DA = ₹3,144) and employee insurance.
official_perks: Government accommodation in GSI staff colonies across regional centers or HRA
Special Field Allowance and Daily Allowance (DA on tour) during remote geological and geophysical survey deployments
Comprehensive medical treatment under Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and annual paid leave
Defined contribution benefits under National Pension System (NPS) with 14% government contribution and central gratuity
